subject: Tiered cooperation & evidence boundaries for suspected data exposure — QuoraMed
messages:
From: Oliver Reed <oliver.reed@quoramed.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.inference.com>
Cc: security@quoramed.com, legal@quoramed.com
Date: Sat, 30 May 2026 17:17:00 +00:00
Subject: Possible exposure of user export file — quick heads up

Ben / Redwood team,

Quick heads-up — our monitoring flagged an anomalous export from a production bucket that may contain a limited set of patient identifiers tied to a small cohort of clinical study participants. We’ve quarantined the export and revoked the token, but we need to understand next steps under the DPA and how Redwood intends to cooperate with our forensic review.

What we need from you right now:
- Confirmation of whether Redwood observed any delivery or unintended downstream transfers.
- A list of subprocessors that had access to the affected key during the 72-hour window.
- A short timeframe for when you can provide logs and a manifest we can ingest.

I’m copying QuoraMed security + legal. This is time-sensitive; ideally a preliminary reply within 6 hours so we can triage with regulators.

Thanks,
Oliver Reed
Head of Security — QuoraMed
oliver.reed@quoramed.com

(attachment: export_manifest_preview.csv)

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.inference.com>
To: Oliver Reed <oliver.reed@quoramed.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.inference.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.inference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.inference.com>
Date: Sat, 30 May 2026 11:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Possible exposure of user export file — quick heads up

Oliver — thanks for the alert and for quarantining the export. We take these reports seriously. Quick answers and next steps from our side:

What we can confirm now:
- No evidence yet of data egress to any external endpoint outside of QuoraMed’s targeted export operation. Our ingestion logs show the export call originated from your service account at 2026-05-29T22:11:43Z; token was invalidated at 2026-05-30T01:02:10Z.
- We are pulling access logs and a KV/cache snapshot for the affected instance. Expect an initial manifest and logs (redacted PII where required) within 8 hours.

Requests / clarifications from QuoraMed needed for coordination:
1) Please confirm the minimal set of fields you consider sensitive here (patient id, study id, date of birth, etc.) so we can limit the export for forensic review.
2) Is there an internal legal hold or regulator notification already started on your side?

Proposed cooperation cadence (draft MAP):
- 0–8h: Initial confirmation + manifest and truncated logs (we will redact full identifiers per contract unless you request otherwise).
- 8–48h: Deeper KV/cache snapshot and subprocessors access list for the 72h window.
- 48–120h: Forensic handoff (encrypted archive) under limited access terms; propose read-only escrow with a signed access attestation.

Kimberly and Jordan — can you confirm the DPA timelines we’ve committed to for QuoraMed and whether the EU-specific transfer clause requires any extra steps?

Ben
Ben Carter
Senior Sales Ops — Redwood Inference
(attachment: redwood_initial_ack.txt)

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.inference.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.inference.com>, Oliver Reed <oliver.reed@quoramed.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.inference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.inference.com>
Date: Sat, 30 May 2026 12:37:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Possible exposure of user export file — quick heads up

Thanks, Ben and Oliver.

Contractual framing and practical constraints: per QuoraMed’s DPA annex (Section 5.2 / Notification & Cooperation), Redwood is required to notify within 72 hours of becoming aware of a breach that materially affects our processing of QuoraMed data. Our internal policy layers an initial operational reply within 8 hours (ack + manifest) and a fuller disclosure within 72 hours if the scope escalates.

Important notes:
- Scope: We should treat this as a "limited-scope exposure" until QuoraMed confirms broader impact. That allows us to share a manifest and subsetted logs immediately while preserving full forensic snapshots pending a legal request.
- Subprocessors: We will provide the list of active subprocessors by environment and roles (e.g., telemetry, backups, managed infra). Note that some infra providers are governed by separate SCCs; we will flag any cross-border transfer obligations.
- Evidence transfer: Redwood can provide an encrypted forensic archive to a QuoraMed-designated custodian. For EU-regulated PII, we propose using a staged transfer (SFTP over a presigned, time-limited link) with proof-of-receipt and an access log.

Operational asks for QuoraMed legal/security team: please confirm which of the following you will sign so we can release sensitive-level artifacts:
A) Standard forensic NDA (we can share a template)
B) Limited access attestation (defines who at QuoraMed will have decryption keys and for what purposes)
C) Confirmation whether you will engage a third-party forensic vendor (if yes, provide vendor name & contract id so we can validate subprocessors)

I will prepare a short MAP doc and attach it to the thread; Ben, Jordan — I’ve flagged the EU transfer questions for review.

Kimberly Park
Head of Legal Ops — Redwood Inference
(attachment: legal_ops_map_template.docx)

From: Oliver Reed <oliver.reed@quoramed.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.inference.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.inference.com>
Cc: legal@quoramed.com, security@quoramed.com
Date: Sat, 30 May 2026 15:03:00 +00:00
Subject: Re: Possible exposure of user export file — quick heads up

Kimberly / Ben — thanks for the clarity. Quick responses:

- QuoraMed treats patient PII as sensitive for this cohort (patient_id, dob, study_id, contact email). Please limit exports to hashed ids where possible.
- Legal has not yet opened a formal regulator notification; we’re triaging internally but want to preserve a 72-hour window to determine regulator filing needs.
- We will sign a forensic NDA and limited access attestation; confirm you can provide your NDA template and we’ll review.
- We intend to use an external forensic vendor (Kestrel Forensics). I’ll DM their contract reference and point of contact; please call out any subprocessor overlap.

I’ve uploaded the manifest + the suspicious export sample to a shared folder (link below). We need the manifest redaction guidance you mentioned and the subprocessor list by the end of the day.

Shared evidence link: https://drive.google.com/drive/fake-share-QuoraMed-evidence

Oliver
Oliver Reed
Head of Security — QuoraMed
(attachment: export_sample_snippet.txt)

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.inference.com>
To: Oliver Reed <oliver.reed@quoramed.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.inference.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.inference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.inference.com>
Date: Sat, 30 May 2026 08:42:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Possible exposure of user export file — quick heads up

Oliver — attaching the draft Mutual Action Plan and a minimal manifest we can produce immediately. High level MAP milestones (short):

1) Immediate (0–8h): Redwood to deliver a redacted manifest (fields: record_id hash, export_timestamp, source_cluster, operator_id) and a timeline of token use.
2) Short (8–48h): Subprocessors access roster (roles only), KV/cache snapshot for the affected instance, and list of retention buckets.
3) Medium (48–120h): Encrypted forensic archive for QuoraMed custodian under NDA + read-only access; transfer via presigned SFTP link.
4) Closure (up to 21 days): Joint write-up for regulator filing if QuoraMed decides notification is required; we’ll preserve all logs and provide an audit trail.

Please confirm acceptance of the MAP and the named Kestrel vendor so we can route the escrow and sign the NDA.

Attachments: mutual_action_plan_v1.docx (stub), forensic_snapshot_manifest.txt (stub)

Ben
Ben Carter
Senior Sales Ops — Redwood Inference
Redwood Inference | ben_carter@redwood.inference.com
